Direct-to-S3 presigned upload:

- SongStoragePort exposes generateUploadUrl/confirmUpload with value objects
- No file bytes through the API; client PUTs directly to S3 presigned URL

Testing:
- Added handleForbiddenException_shouldReturn403 to GlobalExceptionHandlerTest
- Refactored PlaylistFlowIT to self-contained user registration per test
- Fixed ArtistSongFlowIT presigned URL PUT (RestAssured double-encodes query
  params; switched to JDK HttpClient to preserve URL encoding)

Docs: CHANGELOG, README, lessons and testing-playbook synced.

All 130 tests pass with ./mvnw clean test.
Harden backend security: fix IDOR, user enumeration, mass assignment, CORS, add rate limiting

fix: 71 verified bugs from a full-stack adversarial hunt (v21.10)

Six finder sweeps over disjoint areas, every candidate finding tried by a
skeptic before it counted: 83 candidates, 5 refuted, 71 fixed (a pie-label
clip was caught visually after the sweep). Highlights:

- Postgres deploys were unusable: SQLite-only INSERT OR IGNORE and
  GROUP_CONCAT 500'd auth and the dataset list; the $N->? rewrite mis-bound
  repeated placeholders (libsql binds NULL silently) — named binding now.
- IDORs closed: user-scoped analysis cache key; membership/ownership guards
  on dashboards, widgets, comments, activity, and folder routes.
- Stats correctness: listwise deletion restores row pairing for paired-t /
  correlation / regression / Cronbach; PLS-SEM refuses blank cells instead
  of imputing 0; constant-y regression no longer reports r2=1 p=0; real
  seeded reservoir sampling; Welford co-moments kill catastrophic
  cancellation; scatter plots the configured x-vs-y pair.
- Behavior: scheduler persists a computed next_run (was firing every
  minute forever); rate-limit windows actually reset; multi-upload
  validates before writing storage and returns from the handler; permanent
  delete removes the stored bytes; share unlock clears needsPass; modal
  focus trap no longer re-arms per keystroke; pie labels get headroom.
- agent.test.js assertion updated: the budget-exhausted final call must
  keep tools + tool_choice none — omitting tools 400s on the real API.

Verified: 314 unit + 238 integration + e2e + 27 browser + 32 frontend
tests pass; production build clean; key flows re-checked live in-browser.

explanation:
feat(sales): ticket priority — pick on create, change after filing

Sales agents can now set a Zoho Desk priority when filing a ticket and change
it afterwards. Verified against the live org: `priority` is a standard
(non-custom) picklist on the tickets module with the members `-None-`, `Low`,
`Medium`, `High` — case-sensitive, and this org has no `Urgent`.

Backend
- createDeskTicket sends `priority` TOP-LEVEL, not under `cf` (it is not a
  custom field). Omitted when the agent leaves it at None.
- New `PATCH /v1/desk/tickets/:id/priority` → Desk `PATCH /tickets/{id}`.
  Owner-scoped through the existing assertTicketOwned IDOR guard, so a rep may
  only re-prioritise tickets they created, and audited as
  `desk.ticket.priority.update`.
- The change route accepts Desk's `-None-` member so a priority can be cleared;
  create simply omits the field instead.

Frontend
- Create wizard: priority segmented control (None default / Low / Medium / High).
- New "Your recent tickets" strip under the wizard — the only surface that reads
  Desk tickets while the Tickets tab is parked. Each row's priority opens a
  select-shaped dropdown; the pick is staged behind a confirmation modal and the
  row only shows the new value once Desk accepts it.

Timeout fix
- The Desk token has no `Desk.search.READ` scope, so the ticket list falls back
  to scanning recent org tickets. The full 100-page sweep measured 27.6s and
  tripped the client's 20s timeout ("The backend took too long to respond").
  Added an optional `scan_pages` bound to the list route; the strip asks for 10
  pages (~3.8s worst case, ~1s once a match is found). Granting the search scope
  removes the scan entirely and is the real fix.

Tests: 6 new desk-route cases (top-level not cf, omitted when unset, casing and
non-members rejected, owner-scoped PATCH, clearing to -None-).

explanation:
Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the

fix(events): unstick cross-tenant admins from registration, waitlist and roster

Closes the corner 766b867d2 deliberately left open. Registration was held back
because its semantics really are different from attendance — the actor is
usually a member acting on themselves, not a policy-gated manager. Reading it
properly showed the path has THREE people in it, following different rules, and
only one of them was wrong.

1) The ACTOR is global, and four lookups tenant-scoped it, so any manager whose
account row lives on another tenant (network admins, platform admins) was
refused approve/reject/cancel, the bulk people endpoint, the waitlist and the
roster:

- EventRegistrationController::actor()
- the persisted-actor re-read in EventRegistrationService::lockActor()
- the same re-read in EventWaitlistService::lockActor()
- the actor-tenant comparison in EventPeopleService::assertActorScope()

Fixing only the controller would have changed nothing: two of the four are
re-reads that refuse again AFTER authorisation has been granted, the trap called
out in 766b867d2.

Root Cause: the acting user's own identity lookup was tenant-scoped. Auth is
global in this codebase; only resources are tenant-scoped.

Prevention: the actor resolves by authenticated id alone (no IDOR risk — the id
comes from requireUserId()); authority is still decided by
EventPolicy::manageRegistration against the tenant-scoped event, and event,
subject, registration and waitlist-entry lookups stay tenant-scoped.

2) The SUBJECT stays same-tenant, and that is now documented rather than
looking like the bug. EventsController::legacyRegistrationActor() keeps its
tenant predicate: all four of its call sites pass the authenticated id as BOTH
actor and subject (self-service RSVP / waitlist), and a participation subject
must belong to the event's tenant — EventParticipationEligibilityService,
"the boundary for every writer", enforces exactly that
(event_participation_scope_invalid) and then runs safeguarding contact checks
that are tenant-local by construction. Dropping the predicate would have changed
no outcome; the subject lookup in lockParticipants() refuses the same caller a
moment later. A comment at the lookup records this, and
EventRegistrationController now splits actor() (global, management) from
selfActor() (same-tenant, self-service) so the rule is visible in code. The
split also keeps a cross-tenant member's refusal a truthful 403 rather than the
404 "member not found" the subject lookup would raise deeper in the stack.

3) NOT FIXED, and pinned by a test that says so:
EventParticipationEligibilityService resolves the event's ORGANIZER with
AND tenant_id = ? before the safeguarding checks, so an event created by a
cross-tenant organiser accepts no registrations at all — including a local
member registering themselves. 5373940c8 made that event creatable and
publishable, so it is reachable. It is left alone because the fix is not simply
dropping the predicate: SafeguardingInteractionPolicy exposes
assertCrossTenantContactAllowed() as a distinct evaluation from
assertLocalContactAllowed(), so resolving the organizer globally while still
calling the local check would skip a safeguarding boundary rather than honour
it. That is an owner decision, and
test_event_owned_by_a_cross_tenant_organizer_still_refuses_registration will
fail the moment it changes.

fix(events): unstick cross-tenant organisers and admins from event check-in

The last corner of the bug class cleared by 5373940c8: four ACTOR lookups
on the attendance path resolved the acting user with `AND tenant_id = ?`
against the event's tenant, so a platform admin, network admin, or the
event's own cross-tenant organiser was refused check-in / attendance
marking with event_attendance_authorization_denied:

- EventService::attendanceActor() (markAttended + bulk marking)
- EventsController::attendanceActor() (the v2 check-in endpoints)
- the persisted-actor re-read inside EventAttendanceService::record()
- the persisted-actor re-read inside EventAttendanceService::transition()

Fixing only the outer attendanceActor() would have changed nothing: the
service re-read the actor with the same predicate and refused again.

Root Cause: the acting user's own identity lookup was tenant-scoped. Auth
is global in this codebase; only resources are tenant-scoped.

Prevention: the actor resolves by authenticated id alone (no IDOR risk —
the id comes from the authenticated session); authority is still decided
by EventPolicy::manageAttendance against the tenant-scoped event, and
event/attendee/registration lookups stay tenant-scoped. Six regression
tests in EventAttendanceCrossTenantActorTest assert the services directly
(Sanctum::actingAs masks cross-tenant behaviour); the three positive cases
were verified to fail against the old predicate, and the stranger,
suspended-actor and foreign-event guards hold under both versions.

EventsController::legacyRegistrationActor() carries the same predicate but
has different authorization semantics (self-registration, not policy-gated
management) — deliberately left out of scope, flagged for its own review.

GHSA-pxmc-2ffp-8j67: prevent arbitrary certificate revocation via duplicate DB rows

Certificate identity was tracked only by Lemur's internal database row, not
by the actual CA-side certificate. Any authenticated user could upload a
duplicate record for a certificate they didn't own (matching an existing
authority_id and serial) and then revoke it, causing the CA to revoke the
real certificate belonging to another user.

- POST /api/1/certificates/upload now requires AuthorityPermission on the
  specified authority, and rejects uploads whose (authority_id, serial)
  pair already matches an existing certificate (409).
- PUT /api/1/certificates/<id>/revoke now checks authorization and endpoint
  attachment against every certificate row sharing (authority_id, serial)
  with the one being revoked, not just the row named in the request.

Require authorization on certificates referenced via replaces/replacements

The replaces/replacements field on certificate create, upload, and edit
requests let an authenticated caller reference an arbitrary certificate
by ID without any ownership or role check, silencing its expiration
notifications and retargeting its rotation. Enforce the same
CertificatePermission check used for direct revoke/edit on every
certificate named in replaces before the request is processed.

## What this is

NovelTea is a self-hosted, offline-first long-form writing app, Scrivener-shaped: a binder tree, document snapshots, labels/statuses, custom metadata, saved/smart collections, and compile presets. Clients are web, Tauri (Windows/macOS), and iOS. Every client keeps a full local replica and works fully disconnected.

Copyright Anthony Carlascio. This repo is the **open core** under Elastic License 2.0; commercial features live in a separate private repo (see Editions).

- **`WireEnumTest`** drives off the enum constants themselves, so a new value is covered the moment it is added: round-tripping, unique lowercase wire forms, case and whitespace tolerance, and empty (never an exception) for null, blank, unknown and injection-shaped input.
- **`EnumSchemaAlignmentTest`** reads the allowed values out of `pg_constraint` and compares them to the enum, then writes every value to the real table. The enum and the CHECK constraint are two declarations of one fact in different languages; nothing but this keeps them honest. Add a value to one and not the other and it fails, naming the constraint.

## Compile

`packages/compile` turns ProseMirror documents into the formats Core ships (`txt`, `md`, `html`). `ExportProvider` on the Java side reports the same boundary; a commercial module contributes the remaining formats by supplying another implementation, and Core must keep working with only its own provider present.

### binder_item

The tree structure — folders, documents, trash. This is the Scrivener "binder."

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

| type | enum | `folder` \| `document` \| `trash` |
| title | text | |
| order_index | float | fractional indexing — lets you reorder/insert without rewriting siblings *(superseded — see A4)* |
| icon | text, nullable | optional custom icon (Scrivener-style) |
| deleted_at | timestamptz, nullable | soft delete — needed for sync tombstones |
| version | bigint | monotonic, incremented on every change |
| updated_by_device_id | uuid | for conflict attribution |

| id | uuid | same as binder_item.id, or separate FK — recommend same id for simplicity |
| content | jsonb | ProseMirror doc JSON |
| word_count | int | derived, cached for fast binder display |
| synopsis | text, nullable | the Scrivener index-card text |
| notes | text, nullable | document notes (rich text or plain) |
| version | bigint | incremented per content save |
| updated_at | timestamptz | |

### snapshot

Manual or auto point-in-time captures of a document's content (Scrivener's snapshot feature).

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### label / status

Scrivener-style metadata taxonomies, per project.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|

### custom_metadata_field + custom_metadata_value

For arbitrary principal-defined metadata (Scrivener's custom meta-data pane). Field defs at the project level, values keyed per binder_item.

### collection

- Each entity carries a version integer, bumped on every write.
- Client pushes a batch: {entity, base_version, new_data} for each locally-changed record since last sync.
- Server accepts if base_version matches current server version (no one else changed it since the client last knew about it). Otherwise it's a conflict.
- On conflict for document content: don't try to merge rich text — create a sibling binder_item titled "<original title> (Conflicted Copy, <device>, <timestamp>)" containing the client's version, and let the principal manually reconcile. This mirrors Dropbox/Scrivener's own real-world behavior and avoids building a merge algorithm for rich text, which is a rabbit hole.
- On conflict for tree structure (moves/renames/reorders): last-write-wins by server timestamp is fine — much lower stakes than losing prose.
- Sync trigger: client-side connectivity monitor starts a 15-minute timer on regaining connection; only fires sync if the connection holds for the full window (resets on drop). Manual "sync now" button always available as an override.

Allowlist link schemes, sweep every route for IDOR, drop product names

Fixes a real cross-site scripting hole in compiled output. Link hrefs were
escaped but their scheme was never checked, so a document containing
javascript:alert(1) produced a working anchor in every format that carries
links. Escaping cannot help there: the payload contains nothing that needs
escaping. isSafeHref now allowlists http, https, mailto and relative
references, normalising away case, whitespace and control characters first so
JaVaScRiPt: and an embedded tab do not slip past, and failing closed on schemes
nobody has listed. An unsafe link loses its anchor, keeps its text, and warns.
Markdown gets the same treatment, since markdown links execute in renderers.

IdorSweepTest enumerates every route from the handler mapping and drives each
one with a stranger's token. Routes naming another account's resource must not
answer 2xx; caller-scoped collections may, but must not contain the victim's
data; nothing may answer 500; and the victim's project must be unchanged
afterwards. Reading the mapping rather than a hand-written list means a new
controller method that forgets its authorization check fails immediately.

Removes third-party product names from tracked files, replacing them with
descriptions of the behaviour they referred to.

fix(red-team): address 8 security vulnerabilities from Red Team audit

1. ATTACK-01: Fake promo codes → database-backed validation with PromoCode model + migration 021
2. ATTACK-04: XSS in email → html.escape() + URL scheme validation on all user-controlled fields
3. ATTACK-05: CSRF bypass → extended CSRF protection to all mutating endpoints (with webhook/auth exempts)
4. ATTACK-06: Entitlement race condition → atomic UPDATE with WHERE clause (consumed+qty <= quantity)
5. ATTACK-09: IDOR in prompt compiler → pass user_id to compile_prompt, verify project ownership
6. ATTACK-15: Mock payment mode → startup guard raises if YOOKASSA creds missing in production
7. ATTACK-16: Audit log silent bypass → changed logger.debug to logger.warning
8. ATTACK-19: Missing security headers → added SecurityHeadersMiddleware (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
9. ATTACK-20: Contact import validation → added input validation, length limits, date parsing, contacts limit

RED TEAM SCORE: 22/100 → estimated improvement to 65/100

* wt/m4-135:
  test(api): make the revocation barrier valid under RefreshDatabase
  refactor(api): keep the human-only verbs out of tool copy
  fix(api): audit MCP writes that wrote, not retries that did not
  docs(api): document the MCP env flags in .env.example
  fix(api): close the remaining MCP write gaps from the codex gate
  fix(api): resolve the MCP gate and its ingress limiter ahead of the guard
  docs: close the two #131 debts deferred to the MCP server
  feat(web): gate the agent-token panel on the mcp capability
  test(api): add the MCP-token role row to the IDOR matrix
  feat(api): serve read + comment MCP tools to agent reviewers
  feat(api): gate the MCP surface on its own flag, independent of AI

fix(api): close the agent-token gaps found by the codex gate

Critical: the MCP-only rule was scoped to the /api/v1 prefix, so POST /logout —
the one root-level auth:sanctum route — still accepted agent bearers, giving an
agent a human-only action and a token-validity oracle. The refusal now sits on
both route groups; accepting a token is a positive capability exactly one
surface will opt into (#135). The IDOR sweep enumerates every registered route
instead of a prefix, and proves its two exemptions authenticate nothing.

High: Sanctum's provider hoists EnsureFrontendRequestsAreStateful to the front
of the middleware priority list at boot, which sorted the session/CSRF stack
ahead of the refusal — a bearer with a first-party Origin opened a database
session and hit 419 before being refused. AppServiceProvider now hoists the
refusal after Sanctum's provider; asserted on pipeline order and as zero
queries on a rejected request. Mint and its audit record are one transaction;
revoke records through recordSafely and only the request that removed the row
records an event; the Policy trait fails closed on any persistent token that is
not an AgentToken.

Also: no-store on the mint response, a dismiss action for the revealed value,
error-vs-empty on the settings list, deny-as-not-found for a foreign token id,
and a per-member token cap that bounds the unpaginated list.

Dismissals and deferrals recorded in TODOS.md.

explanation:
Connect Supabase as the live database and fix critical security/data bugs

Repoints Eloquent from local MySQL to Supabase Postgres (the actual
production database), then fixes the real bugs that surfaced once the
app was actually exercised end-to-end against it:

- Locks down anon-role database access: every table had unrestricted
  read/write/delete via the exposed Supabase anon key, including the
  users table (password hashes). Revoked access to internal tables and
  restricted app tables to the exact operations the frontend uses.
- Fixes users.id having no default/sequence at all, which made every
  registration fail with a not-null violation.
- Removes a dead `section` text column on users that shadowed the
  section() relationship, silently breaking teacher approval of
  students (always evaluated to null, so ownership checks always
  failed).
- Fixes real IDOR: a teacher could approve/reject/reset any student
  platform-wide, not just their own section's.
- Stops leaking the AI API key to the browser; proxies quiz generation
  through the server instead.
- Rebuilds teacher/admin/student analytics from real Supabase data
  instead of hardcoded zeros, rand(), and a disconnected admin_users
  table that was never actually used by auth.
- Fixes silent quiz-publish duplication (missing unique constraint
  meant "replace" actually inserted a duplicate row).
- Adds unclosed-<script> and broken-relationship fixes found via live
  browser testing, plus 30+ new feature tests covering the above.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: honest refusals instead of raw 500s when the study database is absent (#108)

POST /api/practice/quiz/start and GET /api/gbrain/mock-exam/:sessionId returned a raw "Internal server error" without DATABASE_URL, and the mock-exam body echoed the store's internal "DATABASE_URL not configured" string to the student. Both now return 503 with an honest sentence.

A failed XP read is deliberately not degraded to 0: falling through to the 422 would tell a student they have not practised enough when the true state is that their progress cannot be read.

The mock-exam ownership lookup is wrapped and fails closed, because it is the control that closed the IDOR on keyed sessions; a database error must never read as "no owner yet, proceed". An explicit DATABASE_URL guard runs ahead of it so no internal string can reach a student through the generation catch.

Four tests, including a no-leak assertion on the response body and the fail-closed property that generation never runs when ownership cannot be established.

fix: auditoria completa — segurança, bugs críticos e infra

Correções de segurança:
- hash de senha PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 com salt (era SHA-256 puro sem salt),
  com migração automática de contas legadas no login
- IDOR corrigido em applications/resumes/notifications/calendar (404 se
  o recurso não pertence ao usuário autenticado)
- estado do OAuth do LinkedIn agora expira e tem teto de entradas; login
  sem client id/secret retorna 503 em vez de gerar URL quebrada
- FRONTEND_URL do redirect pós-OAuth configurável (não mais hardcoded)

Bugs corrigidos:
- MissingGreenlet em job.company (lazy-load async) causava 500 em
  Match, ATS Score, Carta e Auto Apply — corrigido com eager loading
- import do GitHub usava endpoint errado (/user/repos em vez de
  /users/{username}/repos), nunca trazia os repos certos
- embedding fallback gerava inf/NaN (bytes de hash como float32 cru)
- lifespan do FastAPI nunca era registrado — tabelas não eram criadas
  automaticamente no start em dev
- chamadas LLM sem timeout travavam a requisição indefinidamente;
  agora têm timeout configurável e falham com 502 em vez de pendurar
- notificação por e-mail enviava o UUID do usuário como destinatário
- UUID/status/data inválidos causavam 500 em vez de 422
- portas fixas no docker-compose colidiam com serviços locais
- init.sql quebrava o boot do Postgres sem a extensão pgvector
- sessão do frontend não persistia entre reloads
- ESLint quebrado (config v8 com pacote ESLint v9)
- numpy usado mas ausente de requirements.txt
- primeira migration Alembic real gerada (schema não tinha nenhuma)

🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix IDOR / State Override in phase transitions

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: WebSocket handlers for ROUND_END, SHOP_FINISH, and SHOP_ENTER accepted full player state arrays from any client slot without verifying authorization, allowing any client to forcefully overwrite the entire game roster's health, money, and inventory.
🎯 Impact: A malicious unprivileged client could exploit this IDOR/State Override vulnerability to manipulate the global game state, dictate match winners, or grant themselves infinite resources at the expense of others.
🔧 Fix: Added explicit authorization checks (`slot !== 0`) before processing these authoritative full-roster snapshots, ensuring only the host client can dictate phase transitions.
✅ Verification: Tested via unit tests for GameRoom Durable Object; ensuring invalid fire commands and unauthorized transitions are correctly rejected.

Add multi-tenant support: multiple restaurants, one system

Every restaurant's data is now isolated by a new Restaurant model —
tables, comandas, menu, orders, payments, coupons, help calls, audit
log and staff all carry a restaurantId and are scoped by it end to
end. This is the foundation for self-service onboarding ("reach the
market") and for a future iFood/delivery-platform channel to slot in
next to KIOSK/DELIVERY/SCHEDULED.

Architecture:
- New `Restaurant` model (id, slug, createdAt). `Settings` keyed by
  restaurantId instead of a hardcoded "singleton" row.
- QR tokens (table/comanda) and the Checkout id stay globally unique
  on purpose — that's how an anonymous QR scan resolves its own
  restaurant with no slug/login needed. Human-facing numbers (table
  number, comanda number, order number/pickup ticket, coupon code)
  become unique per restaurant instead of globally.
- User.email stays globally unique (keeps /login simple: no
  restaurant selection before the password prompt).
- Every by-id staff mutation (delete/update) now scopes on
  {id, restaurantId} via deleteMany/updateMany + a count check,
  instead of trusting a bare id — closes an IDOR class of bug that a
  single-tenant system never had to worry about.
- Realtime SSE topics ("kitchen"/"pdv") are now per-restaurant
  (`kitchen:${restaurantId}`) so one restaurant's live board never
  sees another's events.
- /totem and /pedir move to /totem/[slug] and /pedir/[slug] — the only
  public screens with no QR Code to resolve a restaurant from. New
  /signup does self-service onboarding (Restaurant + Settings + first
  ADMIN user, auto-login), also used as the isolation test's own
  second-tenant fixture.
- Data migration backfills all pre-existing rows onto one
  'rst_default' restaurant (slug "principal") — the real restaurant
  already in production, preserved verbatim.

Found and fixed during isolation testing: the order-number Counter
row wasn't migrated to its new per-restaurant key, so the first order
placed after the migration collided with an existing order number
(unique constraint violation). Added a small follow-up migration that
renames the counter key, preserving the existing sequence.

Verified: full TypeScript + lint clean, production build clean. A
12-point isolation test (via /signup, creating a real second
restaurant on an isolated DB copy) confirms: empty dashboards for a
new tenant, 404 on cross-tenant IDOR attempts by id, independent
per-restaurant numbering/coupons/audit log, SSE events never leaking
across restaurants, and /totem/[slug] serving only its own menu.
Separately reran the full real-restaurant regression (QR order → PDV
payment → totem → painel → reports) after the fix.

fix(security): AuthPrincipal.userId ở certificates/grading + chặn quyền rỗng

Lỗi có sẵn từ P5, phát hiện khi verify P7 (KHÔNG do P7 gây ra).

Gốc: `@CurrentUser()` trả `AuthPrincipal { userId }`, nhưng certificates.service.ts và
grading.service.ts khai kiểu `AuthUser` rồi đọc `currentUser.id` / `currentUser.roles`
→ luôn undefined lúc chạy. Hậu quả đã xác nhận trên DB dev:

- `getEffectivePermissions(undefined)` → `userRole.findMany({ where: { userId: undefined } })`
  — Prisma coi undefined là "không lọc" → trả MỌI user_role → hợp nhất quyền của mọi role
  ≈ super_admin. Mọi kiểm quyền trong certificates đều pass.
- `listMine` lọc `userId: undefined` → trả chứng chỉ của MỌI học viên.
- `POST /certificates/:id/revoke` và `GET /certificates/:id/pdf` (chỉ JwtAuthGuard, scope
  kiểm trong service) → user bất kỳ thu hồi / tải được chứng chỉ người khác.
- `GET /classes/:classId/my-gradebook` ném 500 PrismaClientValidationError.

Sửa:
- certificates + grading nhận `AuthPrincipal` và dùng `currentUser.userId`. Bỏ shortcut
  `currentUser.roles?.includes('admin')` — admin/super_admin nhận quyền ở phạm vi GLOBAL
  nên `hasPermission` đã phủ (đối chiếu seed: cả hai có certificate.*/grade.read).
- `RbacService.getEffectivePermissions` trả quyền RỖNG khi userId falsy, không chạm DB —
  phòng thủ chiều sâu để một chỗ gọi sai không bao giờ thành cấp quyền toàn hệ thống.
- Test hồi quy (+6): rbac userId rỗng (undefined/null/''), revoke 403 + tra đúng userId,
  listMine lọc đúng userId, getPdfBuffer IDOR 403.

Verify: `pnpm validate` 16/16, api 180 test. Live sau vá: my-gradebook 200; HV không sở hữu
`/certificates/mine` = 0 (chủ sở hữu = 1), `:id/pdf` 403, `:id/revoke` 403; GV vẫn đọc được
`/certificates/class/:id` và `/gradebook` (200).

Ghi nhận nợ MỚI (chưa vá, có từ P6/D1): sinh PDF chứng chỉ 500 với tiếng Việt —

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:
  ✓ returns 401 explicitly when there is no userId

None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

## Risk
Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

Security audit hardening: CORS, rate limiting, DTO validation, httpOnly session cookie, upload content-sniffing

Implements the fixes from this session's full security audit (Sections
5-8 plus remaining Section 3/4 items) that weren't already applied live:

- CORS: replace origin:'*' with an explicit allowlist (APP_URL/
  FRONTEND_URL/localhost) in the production Nest bootstrap
  (apps/web/src/lib/backendPort.ts). The previous config also paired
  wildcard origin with credentials:true, an invalid combination per the
  Fetch spec.

- Rate limiting: add @Throttle overrides on auth endpoints (login/
  register/verify/resend/forgot-password/reset-password) and on the two
  AI-generation endpoints, tighter than the app-wide default limiter.

- Server-side validation: convert ~13 inline @Body() object-literal types
  across auth/engine/media/oauth/posts controllers into real
  class-validator DTO classes, closing a gap where NestJS's global
  ValidationPipe silently validated nothing for non-class body types.

- Session storage: move the auth JWT from localStorage (readable by any
  XSS for up to 30 days) to an httpOnly cookie. AuthController.login sets
  it; a new AuthController.logout clears it. JwtStrategy reads it via a
  hand-rolled cookie parser (no new dependency). The frontend now caches
  only a non-sensitive user snapshot (id/email/name/brandId/expiry) for
  synchronous UI checks; apiFetch, the upload flow, the SSE stream, and
  the three OAuth connect links all rely on the cookie traveling
  automatically instead of a client-readable token.

- File upload content-sniffing: verify uploaded bytes actually match
  their claimed MIME type (magic-byte checks for JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP/
  ISOBMFF/EBML) on both the multer path and the direct-to-Blob register
  path, on top of the existing allowlist checks.

- OAuth error handling: stop reflecting err.message into redirect query
  params (info-disclosure risk); log full errors server-side, show
  generic messages to the user. Remove partial-secret and raw-code
  logging in the Instagram token exchange.

Also includes earlier uncommitted work from this session: the OAuth
state-signature CSRF bypass fix, IDOR fixes (createPost media ownership,
media folder parentId), MediaAsset atomic processing claim, TikTok
webhook signature verification, AI entitlement bypass fix, comment-

explanation:
Fix real vulnerabilities found in a dedicated security audit

Three parallel audits (auth/authz, injection/input-handling, secrets/
infrastructure) covering the whole app, adversarial lens. Fixes:

CRITICAL
- MFA was completely bypassable: the 5-minute "mfa_pending" challenge
  token issued by /auth/login (before a TOTP/backup code is ever
  checked) decoded and passed get_current_user()'s checks exactly like
  a real session token -- anyone with just a password (the one thing
  MFA exists to add a second factor against) could call any
  authenticated endpoint directly with it, no code required, for the
  full 5-minute window. Now explicitly rejected, same pattern as the
  existing "purpose" claim check.

HIGH
- Twilio webhook signature verification failed OPEN (skipped, request
  allowed through) when TWILIO_TOKEN/PUBLIC_BASE_URL were unset --
  now fails closed (503), matching the pattern already used correctly
  for CRON_SECRET/EMAIL_WORKER_SECRET.
- SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET ship with hardcoded, publicly-known placeholder
  defaults with no code-level guard against running with them in
  production (only Render's generateValue: true prevented this on the
  documented deploy path). App now refuses to boot with DEBUG=false if
  either is still its literal default.

MODERATE
- Three IDOR gaps: POST /communications/send's maintenance_update
  template, POST /maintenance/'s unit_id/tenant_id, and POST
  /accounting/expenses' vendor_id all accepted a foreign org's UUID
  with no ownership check, leaking that resource's name/title/status
  back in the response. All now validated against the caller's org.
- Unescaped HTML injection in three outreach-email templates
  (services/lead_service.py) -- lead fields (scraped from public,
  attacker-editable Google Business Profile data, or typed into
  POST /leads with no sanitization) were interpolated into HTML emails
  with no output encoding. Now html.escape()'d for the HTML body
  specifically (plain-text body unaffected).
- SSRF in the lead-scraper's email-discovery fetch
  (workers/tasks/lead_scraping.py) -- a Places listing's self-reported
  website URL was fetched with no scheme/private-IP allowlist and
  followed redirects blindly, so a listing pointed at an internal
  address or a cloud metadata endpoint would have the server fetch it.
  Added an SSRF guard checked on the initial URL and re-checked on
  every redirect hop.
- FastAPI backend sent no security headers at all (X-Frame-Options,
  X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) --
  only the Next.js frontend did, despite security.tsx's copy claiming
  this applies to "every response." Left /docs and /redoc unprotected
  against framing. Added a headers middleware.
- ALLOWED_ORIGINS="*" combined with allow_credentials=True (a plausible
  operator typo in Render's env vars) would silently make CORS reflect
  any origin with credentials -- app now refuses to boot with that
  combination instead.
- Three endpoints doing real, billed AI/scraping work (inspection photo
  AI analysis, the Claude marketing-copy generator, the lead-scrape
  trigger) had zero rate limiting or cost cap beyond role/plan gating --
  a compromised privileged account or a buggy retry loop had no
  built-in ceiling on Anthropic/OpenAI/Google Places billing, and on
  this single-worker server a burst could also stall every other
  tenant's requests. Added reasonable per-minute limits to all three.

Not fixed here, flagged for a follow-up decision (both require either
a schema migration or a product/UX tradeoff, not a mechanical fix):
- Password reset tokens (staff-side /auth/reset-password) are replayable
  within their 30-minute window -- not marked single-use like the
  tenant-portal equivalent already is.
- Rate limiting on login/reset/2FA is per-IP only, no per-account
  lockout/backoff -- a distributed credential-stuffing attempt across
  many source IPs isn't meaningfully throttled today.
- API keys are stored and compared in plaintext (high-entropy,
  infeasible to brute-force, but a DB-level compromise would expose
  live keys directly rather than hashes) -- hashing at rest would need
  a rotation flow since existing keys can't be un-hashed.

explanation:
feat(sales): ticket priority — pick on create, change after filing

Sales agents can now set a Zoho Desk priority when filing a ticket and change
it afterwards. Verified against the live org: `priority` is a standard
(non-custom) picklist on the tickets module with the members `-None-`, `Low`,
`Medium`, `High` — case-sensitive, and this org has no `Urgent`.

Backend
- createDeskTicket sends `priority` TOP-LEVEL, not under `cf` (it is not a
  custom field). Omitted when the agent leaves it at None.
- New `PATCH /v1/desk/tickets/:id/priority` → Desk `PATCH /tickets/{id}`.
  Owner-scoped through the existing assertTicketOwned IDOR guard, so a rep may
  only re-prioritise tickets they created, and audited as
  `desk.ticket.priority.update`.
- The change route accepts Desk's `-None-` member so a priority can be cleared;
  create simply omits the field instead.

Frontend
- Create wizard: priority segmented control (None default / Low / Medium / High).
- New "Your recent tickets" strip under the wizard — the only surface that reads
  Desk tickets while the Tickets tab is parked. Each row's priority opens a
  select-shaped dropdown; the pick is staged behind a confirmation modal and the
  row only shows the new value once Desk accepts it.

Timeout fix
- The Desk token has no `Desk.search.READ` scope, so the ticket list falls back
  to scanning recent org tickets. The full 100-page sweep measured 27.6s and
  tripped the client's 20s timeout ("The backend took too long to respond").
  Added an optional `scan_pages` bound to the list route; the strip asks for 10
  pages (~3.8s worst case, ~1s once a match is found). Granting the search scope
  removes the scan entirely and is the real fix.

Tests: 6 new desk-route cases (top-level not cf, omitted when unset, casing and
non-members rejected, owner-scoped PATCH, clearing to -None-).

explanation:
Fix security findings from the August 2026 penetration tests

Cross-compared two Strix reports (timetify.net black-box, timetify-gcp
white-box) and verified every finding against the source before acting.

Confirmed and fixed:
- No rate limiting on auth endpoints (CRITICAL). Adds scoped DRF throttles
  for login (per-IP AND per-username), register, password reset, sign-up
  availability check and user search. Counters need a cache shared across
  Cloud Run instances, so CACHES is now Redis-if-available / database
  otherwise, with the table created by migration 0035.
- Public GCS bucket with unsigned URLs (HIGH). Media now goes through
  SignedGoogleCloudStorage, which signs via the IAM signBlob API because
  django-storages signs with a local private key that Cloud Run's metadata
  credentials do not have.
- User enumeration on password reset (both reports), login, and friend
  search. Constant response, generic auth error, 3-char search floor.
- Cross-tenant IDOR via writable `course` FK on Week/Exam/Assignment.
- Case-variant username/email collisions at sign-up, closing the gap left
  by fad745ab, backed by DB constraints rather than serializer checks alone.
- Prompt injection in the AI moderation pipeline: untrusted text is now
  delimited data placed after the instructions, with the output contract
  restated afterwards, plus an injection tripwire.
- Past-dated events, admin on a fixed path, missing CSP/HSTS/frame headers.

Not fixed, because they are not real: the three IDOR findings against the
schedule, notifications and events endpoints. All three views derive the
user from request.user and never read the user_id parameter; Django ignores
the unknown param and returns the caller's own data, which the scanner read
as a cross-user breach.

Also found while verifying, in neither report:
- /api/token/ was SimpleJWT's stock view, bypassing every protection on
  /api/login/ and silently defeating the rate-limiting fix.
- Any nginx location declaring add_header drops the inherited server-level
  ones, which would have voided the new CSP on every HTML response.
- CourseSerializer.parent_course had the same unvalidated-FK hole.
- Moderation auto-enforced on a single model vote despite its docstring
  promising unanimity.
- Password reset matched email case-sensitively.

Dependencies: npm 4 high -> 0; Django 6.0.2 (26 advisories) -> 6.0.7, plus
gunicorn, python-dotenv and pg8000. pip-audit and check --deploy both clean.

Adds 23 regression tests; full suite 162 passing.

Audit of meeting-note-mcp (4 dimensions). Fixes the chosen batch; privacy/
retention (content in mcp_tool_call), token `scopes` enforcement, and dep bumps
were deferred by decision.

Security:
- S1 admin dashboard now FAILS CLOSED when no admin allowlist is configured.
  Previously requireAdmin returned the caller as admin when both MCP_ADMIN_EMAILS
  and MCP_ADMIN_MICROSOFT_IDS were unset (with mcpAdminTenantId defaulting to
  'common'), so any Microsoft account in any tenant could read every user's
  meeting content via /admin. (dashboard.ts)
- S2 get_project_context IDOR closed: dropped the unscoped fetchProjectRowsByIds
  fallback that returned ANY project by id (name + created_at + full note-id list)
  for an enumerable numeric id. Only an owned project row is surfaced now; a
  merely-accessible project derives name/noteIds from the access-scoped notes.
  (projects.ts)

Date correctness (users are in Korea):
- D1 bare YYYY-MM-DD date filters are now interpreted in a configurable IANA zone
  (MCP_DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE, default Asia/Seoul) instead of UTC, so get_notes_by_date
  et al. no longer return the wrong calendar day for KST. search_notes (RPC) picks
  this up via the resolved bounds too. (dateFilters.ts, env.ts)
- R4 startDate/endDate now reject junk ("2026", "May", "2026-13-40") instead of
  lenient new Date() coercion into a wrong-but-valid filter. (dateFilters.ts)

Reliability:
- R1 added AbortSignal.timeout(8000) to every outbound fetch (Graph /me on the
  auth hot path, admin Graph + local health, Resend); Graph lookups now fail
  closed instead of hanging. (http.ts, dashboard.ts, alerts.ts)
- R2 null-guard each note_insight actions/events element so a [null] row can't
  crash find_action_items / find_events. (context.ts)
- R3 stop ignoring the note_insight query error and log the noteAccessOrExpression
  catch, so silent degradation is observable. (context.ts, supabase.ts)
- R5 null-safe project name sort/render in list_projects. (projects.ts)

Scale / honesty signals:
- D2 get_speaker_segments scans diarization-only columns (NOTE_SPEAKER_SCAN_SELECT,
  ~half the bytes vs full transcript select) and now returns reachedNoteCap /
  segmentsTruncated so a capped (silently-incomplete) scan no longer looks
  exhaustive. (notes.ts, supabase.ts)
- D3 list/date/search tools now return hasMore (fetch limit+1 via applyLimitWindow);
  find_action_items/find_events return reachedNoteCap; get_shared_notes_by_owner
  returns reachedScanHorizon. (notes.ts, context.ts, formatters.ts)

- AuditLog: fix a severe cross-tenant leak — core_audit_logs (the real,

  column at all, so any admin-permissioned user could browse every

- Sales: fix the same tenant_id ?? 1 collapse found in Reporting/Strategy,
  plus missing authorization and IDOR exposure on order confirm/cancel.
- Integration: fix two IDOR vulnerabilities — connector actions had zero
  ownership check despite a registered policy sitting unused, and
  WhbPartnerController's approve/reject/suspend had zero tenant scoping
  at all.
- Calendar: policies existed and were called via authorize() but were

  nonexistent controller classes, fatal on every request) and closed a

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Teacher;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Models\User;

class StudentApprovalController extends Controller
{
    public function index(): \Illuminate\View\View
    {
        $pendingStudents = User::where('callerRole', 'student')
            ->where('approval_status', 'pending')
            ->latest()
            ->paginate(15);

        $approvedStudents = User::where('callerRole', 'student')
            ->where('approval_status', 'approved')
            ->latest()
            ->paginate(15);

        $rejectedStudents = User::where('callerRole', 'student')
            ->where('approval_status', 'rejected')
            ->latest()
            ->paginate(15);

        return view('teacher.student-approvals.index', compact('pendingStudents', 'approvedStudents', 'rejectedStudents'));
    }

    public function approve(User $user): \Illuminate\Http\RedirectResponse
    {
        if ($user->callerRole !== 'student') {
            return back()->withErrors(['error' => 'Invalid user callerRole.']);
        }

        $user->update(['approval_status' => 'approved']);

        return back()->with('success', "{$user->name} has been approved and can now log in.");
    }

explanation:
Connect Supabase as the live database and fix critical security/data bugs

Repoints Eloquent from local MySQL to Supabase Postgres (the actual
production database), then fixes the real bugs that surfaced once the
app was actually exercised end-to-end against it:

- Locks down anon-role database access: every table had unrestricted
  read/write/delete via the exposed Supabase anon key, including the
  users table (password hashes). Revoked access to internal tables and
  restricted app tables to the exact operations the frontend uses.
- Fixes users.id having no default/sequence at all, which made every
  registration fail with a not-null violation.
- Removes a dead `section` text column on users that shadowed the
  section() relationship, silently breaking teacher approval of
  students (always evaluated to null, so ownership checks always
  failed).
- Fixes real IDOR: a teacher could approve/reject/reset any student
  platform-wide, not just their own section's.
- Stops leaking the AI API key to the browser; proxies quiz generation
  through the server instead.
- Rebuilds teacher/admin/student analytics from real Supabase data
  instead of hardcoded zeros, rand(), and a disconnected admin_users
  table that was never actually used by auth.
- Fixes silent quiz-publish duplication (missing unique constraint
  meant "replace" actually inserted a duplicate row).
- Adds unclosed-<script> and broken-relationship fixes found via live
  browser testing, plus 30+ new feature tests covering the above.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: honest refusals instead of raw 500s when the study database is absent (#108)

POST /api/practice/quiz/start and GET /api/gbrain/mock-exam/:sessionId returned a raw "Internal server error" without DATABASE_URL, and the mock-exam body echoed the store's internal "DATABASE_URL not configured" string to the student. Both now return 503 with an honest sentence.

A failed XP read is deliberately not degraded to 0: falling through to the 422 would tell a student they have not practised enough when the true state is that their progress cannot be read.

The mock-exam ownership lookup is wrapped and fails closed, because it is the control that closed the IDOR on keyed sessions; a database error must never read as "no owner yet, proceed". An explicit DATABASE_URL guard runs ahead of it so no internal string can reach a student through the generation catch.

Four tests, including a no-leak assertion on the response body and the fail-closed property that generation never runs when ownership cannot be established.

feat: Cohort Operations + Client Briefs + Multimodal Eval Foundation (Issue #16 Phase 1) (#17)

* fix: support markdown submission items end-to-end

- Add MARKDOWN to ItemType enum + PG enum migration (issue #9 §3 requires
  markdown deliverables to remain supported; API previously 500ed)
- update_submission: invalid item type now 422 instead of unhandled 500
- Submit page sends type=markdown for markdown deliverables
- Submission detail + review pages render markdown items with ReactMarkdown

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: instructor review chain — names and links instead of bare ULIDs

- /reviews/pending returns author_name + project_title (joined query)
- Review dashboard shows learner avatar/name, project, full timestamp,
  and an explicit Review CTA per row
- Project submissions list returns author_name; instructors see
  'Submissions' with author identity, learners keep 'My Submissions'
- Workflow status on project detail now derives from MY latest submission
  (was: first row of the org-wide list, wrong for instructors)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: version history UI with notes (issue #9 §7 accessibility of prior versions)

- VersionHistory component: expandable per-deliverable timeline with
  thumbnails, latest badge, timestamps, notes, per-version download
- Wired into submission detail + review pages alongside VersionCompare
- Submit page: optional 'what changed' note input when replacing a file,
  sent as the upload's note field

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: image lightbox — click any image preview to expand

- Lightbox portal component (Esc / backdrop / ✕ close, body scroll lock)
- MediaPreview images are click-to-zoom
- AnnotatedImage zooms when not in drawing mode

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: actionable dashboard + guided submission start

- New /me/overview endpoint: draft submissions, pending peer assessments,
  recent reviews received, and (for instructors) submissions to grade —
  aggregated across orgs
- Dashboard: To-do section + Recent feedback replace API/DB/Cache
  infrastructure status cards (learners see work, not ops)
- Submit page pre-draft state: numbered deliverable checklist with
  type + required badges so learners see the work before starting

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: workflow provenance labels + instructor review CTA

- Workflow stage thumbnails show filename + version
- Submission detail 'No reviews yet' becomes a Start review CTA for
  instructors when the submission is awaiting review

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: ruff format

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: close 9 API vulnerabilities found via adversarial probing

Bug-hunt round on top of the teardown fixes:

- update_submission accepted foreign/bogus deliverable_ids (FK 500),
  cross-project path confusion, phantom file items, and 3MB inline
  content. Now validates deliverable belongs to the project, restricts
  to text/markdown/link, caps content at 100KB, and 404s path mismatch.
- set_project_skills / set_prerequisites inserted unknown or cross-org
  IDs → FK 500 + cross-org data links. Now validate existence + same-org.
- add_member with a nonexistent user_id → FK 500. Now 404.
- create_review allowed reviewing a DRAFT and scores above the project
  maximum. Now 422 on both.
- IDOR: get_download_url did not scope file_id to the submission — a
  user could fetch another submission's file via their own path. Now
  the file must belong to the authorized submission.

Adds 5 adversarial regression tests. Full suite: 646 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: peer-review allocation edge case (num_reviews > pool)

Round 5 adversarial pass on peer review, upload, and prompt subsystems
found no new vulnerabilities — authorization (owner/instructor/allocated
reviewer), state machine (draft/phase), org isolation, and reviewer
anonymity all hold. Adds a regression test for num_reviews exceeding the
reviewable pool (allocator caps at n-1, never self-assigns or duplicates).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: 6 cross-org project-confusion holes (BOLA/IDOR class)

Systematic sweep of all 139 routes with a cross-org probe matrix surfaced
6 project sub-endpoints that verified org membership but NOT that the
project/submission in the URL belongs to that org. A member of org A could
therefore list/create/edit/delete org B's deliverables, list B's
submissions, and submit/delete B's submissions by embedding B's ids in
A's path.

Added _verify_project_org / submission-project checks to:
- GET/POST/PUT/DELETE …/projects/{pid}/deliverables[/{did}]
- GET …/projects/{pid}/submissions
- POST …/submissions/{sid}/submit
- DELETE …/projects/{pid}/submissions/{sid}

Sweeps confirmed skills, exercises, categories, portfolio, evaluation,
and member-management endpoints already scope correctly. Adds a
cross-org confusion regression test. Full suite: 648 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: 7 more input-validation / data-consistency bugs (round 7)

Inline sweep of raw-dict endpoints and cross-field invariants:

- reorder_my_items: item_ids was an unvalidated dict field; non-list/int
  input 500ed. Now a typed ReorderItemsRequest schema (max 500, strings).
- set_project_skills / set_prerequisites: non-list or list-of-non-strings
  500ed the list comprehension. Now 422.
- add_member_directly: non-string user_id (e.g. 123) passed the truthy
  check and hit the FK as an int. Now 422.
- grant_extension: granting to a bogus user 500ed on the FK; granting to
  a real NON-member silently created a phantom extension for an outsider.
  Now validates active org membership → 404.
- Create/UpdateProjectRequest: late_deadline before deadline was accepted,
  producing a negative late window that mis-classifies on-time submits as
  closed. Now rejected via model_validator.

Updates 3 fixtures that relied on the old (buggy) extension behavior.
Adds 3 regression tests. Full suite: 651 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: JSONB persistence + eval settings bounds (round 8)

- update_eval_settings / OrgService.update_settings mutated the nested
  JSONB dict in place. SQLAlchemy's default change-detection compares by
  reference, so the column was never marked dirty and the SECOND update
  to org.settings was silently lost. Rebuild the dict tree so the change
  is detected.
- UpdateEvalSettingsRequest had no bounds: pass_threshold accepted >1 and
  negatives, monthly_budget_usd accepted negatives, default_model empty.
  Now validated (0-1, 0-1M, 1-100 chars).
- get_usage treated a monthly_budget_usd of 0 as "unlimited" (falsy
  check) instead of a real zero budget; budget_remaining now uses
  .

Adds 2 regression tests. Full suite: 653 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: skill progress + MCQ grading correctness (round 9)

- _update_skill_progress counted any GRADED attempt as 'done', so a wrong
  MCQ (score=0, is_correct=False) marked the skill 100% complete and
  unlocked its dependents. Now only PASSED attempts (is_correct=True)
  count — the core learning-gate correctness bug.
- MCQ auto-grader did sorted(user_answer)==sorted(correct) on untrusted
  values; a non-list config.correct (int/dict) or mixed-type selected
  raised TypeError -> 500. Both are now coerced to sorted string lists.
- GradeAttemptRequest had no score/feedback bounds; negative or 10000+
  scores were accepted. Now validated.

Adds 3 regression tests. Full suite: 656 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: portfolio slug collision + profile field bounds (round 10)

- create_item: two items with the same title collide on the (user_id,
  slug) unique index → 500. Now retries with a random slug suffix.
- UpdateProfileRequest had no bounds on headline/bio/location (unbounded
  text into the public page), no visibility enum check, and social_links
  allowed unlimited keys / oversized values. All now validated.

Adds 2 regression tests. Full suite: 658 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: portfolio item + eval-settings input validation (round 11)

- CreatePortfolioItemRequest had no bounds: external_url/cover_image_url
  accepted any scheme (incl. javascript:) and unbounded length — these
  render as href/img src on the PUBLIC profile page (stored-XSS / abuse
  vector). description unbounded, tags unbounded, visibility unvalidated.
  UpdatePortfolioItemRequest was missing the visibility enum check and
  tag bounds too. All now validated (http/https only, lengths, enum).
- Eval settings form sent parseFloat('') → NaN → JSON null, silently
  wiping pass_threshold when the field was blank. Now only sends valid
  numbers and guards NaN for budget.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 659 passed; web type-check clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: invite/member role privilege-escalation guards (round 12)

create_invite_link, invite_members, and add_member_directly checked only
that the actor was instructor+/admin+, not that the GRANTED role was at or
below the actor's own. An instructor could mint an admin/owner invite
link (or email invite) and an admin could directly add an owner —
escalating privilege. All three now reject granting a role higher than
the actor's via ROLE_HIERARCHY.

Adds 2 regression tests. Full suite: 659 + 2 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: eval trigger scoping + unbounded pagination (round 13)

- trigger_evaluation inserted an EvaluationTask with the caller-supplied
  submission_id without any check. A bogus id 500ed on the FK; a
  cross-org submission id ran an eval (and charged the caller's monthly
  budget) against another org's submission. Now validates the submission
  exists and belongs to the org → 404.
- list_eval_tasks and admin list_users used bare  with no
  bounds; page=0/-1 produced a negative SQL OFFSET → 500. Now
  Query(ge=1) / per_page Query(ge=1, le=100), matching the other lists.

Updates 1 unit test for the new submission check. Adds 2 regression
tests. Full suite: 663 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: auth rate limits + last-admin lockout guards (round 14)

- reset-password, verify-email, resend-verification had NO rate limit —
  reset/verify are token brute-force surfaces and resend is an email-bomb
  surface. Added rate_limit (5/15m, 10/15m, 3/15m). (Disabled under
  APP_ENV=test, so no test impact.)
- admin update_user_role / soft_delete_user could demote or delete the
  last active admin, locking the platform out of all admin operations.
  Both now refuse when only one active admin remains.

Full suite: 663 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: public-page url scheme guard + upload-sniffer regression (round 15)

- Public portfolio item page rendered item.external_url as an <a href>
  without a scheme check — a javascript:/data: url stored before the
  create-time validation (or via another path) would execute on click.
  Now the link only renders for http(s) urls (defense in depth alongside
  the create/update validators from round 11).
- Locks in the upload magic-byte sniffer behavior (empty / truncated /
  mime-mismatched uploads → 422, never 500) with a regression test.

Full suite: 664 passed; web type-check clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: deliverable config + type validation (round 16)

CreateDeliverableRequest never validated its type string (unknown types
were only caught later in the service) and neither Create nor Update nor
template deliverables validated config. A garbage max_file_size_mb
(negative), non-int max_files, or non-list accepted_formats was accepted
and then silently disabled the upload size/format enforcement at submit
time — the config *looked* set but did nothing. Added a shared
_validate_deliverable_config (max_files 1-100, max_file_size_mb 1-500,
accepted_formats list of MIME strings) applied to create/update/template
deliverables, plus a type-enum check on create.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 664 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: bound remaining unbounded text/config fields (round 17)

Closes the last unbounded storage surfaces:
- CreateOrgRequest.description (Update had a bound, Create didn't)
- CreateCategoryRequest.description + icon
- CreateExerciseRequest.description + config JSON blob

All now capped, matching the bounds already enforced on their Update
counterparts and sibling schemas.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 666 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: dedup prerequisite / project-skill ids (round 18)

Passing a repeated id in set_prerequisites or set_project_skills inserted
duplicate rows that violate the composite primary key → 500. Both now
de-duplicate (order-preserving) before insert, and flush the delete of the
old set before re-inserting so replacing a set with an overlapping one
doesn't collide within the same transaction. (self-prerequisite and
indirect cycles were already correctly rejected as 422.)

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 667 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: gate submissions on publish + bound extension reason (round 19)

- create_submission never checked project status: a student could create
  submissions against a DRAFT/unpublished (or archived) project, which
  isn't open for work. Now non-instructors get 422 unless the project is
  PUBLISHED; instructors may still submit to a draft to test the flow.
- GrantExtensionRequest.reason was unbounded free text — now capped at
  1,000 chars.

Adds 2 regression tests. Full suite: 669 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: gate exercise attempts on skill publish status (round 20)

submit_attempt only checked prerequisite-unlock, not whether the skill was
published. A student could submit attempts against a DRAFT skill's
exercises (and accrue progress) before the instructor published it. Now
non-instructors get 422 unless the skill is PUBLISHED; instructors may
still attempt a draft skill's exercises to test them. Mirrors the
project-submission publish gate from round 19.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 670 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: revision-requested submissions were a dead end (round 21)

When an instructor set a submission to revision_requested, every edit path
(update_submission, submit_draft, upload_file, add_prompt_item,
delete_file) still gated strictly on status == DRAFT — so the learner
could neither change anything nor resubmit. The whole revision workflow
was unusable. All five paths now accept DRAFT or REVISION_REQUESTED;
APPROVED/REJECTED/SUBMITTED remain locked.

Adds 1 regression test (edit+resubmit works, approved stays locked).
Full suite: 671 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: partial project update could break deadline ordering (round 22)

The late_deadline>=deadline model_validator only fires when both fields
are present in the request. A partial PUT changing only deadline could
push it past an existing late_deadline, producing a negative late window
(same class as round 7, but via the update path). update_project now
re-checks the ordering on the combined post-update values.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 672 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: version collision + max_files slot leak on delete (round 23)

_next_item_version used count(*)+1. After deleting a middle version,
the next upload reused an existing version number (e.g. delete v1 of
[v1,v2] then upload → another v2). Now uses max(version)+1.

Separately, the max_files cap compared the (monotonic) version counter,
so deleting a file never freed a slot — a max_files=2 deliverable stayed
full forever after two uploads even if you deleted one. Now it counts
actual stored items.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 673 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: blank items satisfied required deliverables (round 24)

_validate_required_deliverables treated a deliverable as complete if ANY
item row existed for it — so an empty or whitespace-only text/link/markdown
item let a learner submit a project with required work effectively blank.
Now a deliverable is only satisfied by a file/prompt item or a
text/link/markdown item with non-blank content.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 674 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: inline item edits accumulated duplicate rows (round 25)

update_submission always INSERTed a new SubmissionItem, so editing a
text/markdown/link deliverable N times left N rows — the learner sees
their answer once in the form but stores a growing pile of stale
duplicates, which muddies the reviewer view and the required-deliverable
check. Now an inline item of the same (deliverable, type) is replaced
in place; a new one is inserted only if none exists.

Adds 1 regression test. Full suite: 675 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: prompt-item duplication + S3 leak on submission delete (round 26)

- add_prompt_item always INSERTed, so editing a prompt deliverable piled
  up stale rows (inflating the version counter and corrupting exports/
  audit even though the UI shows only the latest). Now replaces the single
  prompt row in place. Updates the versioning test to assert replace
  semantics.
- delete_submission removed the DB row (items cascade) but never deleted
  the uploaded S3 objects — every deleted draft with files leaked storage
  forever. Now cleans up all file_keys best-effort first.

Adds 2 regression tests. Full suite: 677 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: long filenames 500 on upload; unbounded asset name/description (round 27)

- A client filename >255 chars overflowed the file_name column (DataError
  500); even shorter-but-long names blew the S3 object-name limit MinIO

Add multi-tenant support: multiple restaurants, one system

Every restaurant's data is now isolated by a new Restaurant model —
tables, comandas, menu, orders, payments, coupons, help calls, audit
log and staff all carry a restaurantId and are scoped by it end to
end. This is the foundation for self-service onboarding ("reach the
market") and for a future iFood/delivery-platform channel to slot in
next to KIOSK/DELIVERY/SCHEDULED.

Architecture:
- New `Restaurant` model (id, slug, createdAt). `Settings` keyed by
  restaurantId instead of a hardcoded "singleton" row.
- QR tokens (table/comanda) and the Checkout id stay globally unique
  on purpose — that's how an anonymous QR scan resolves its own
  restaurant with no slug/login needed. Human-facing numbers (table
  number, comanda number, order number/pickup ticket, coupon code)
  become unique per restaurant instead of globally.
- User.email stays globally unique (keeps /login simple: no
  restaurant selection before the password prompt).
- Every by-id staff mutation (delete/update) now scopes on
  {id, restaurantId} via deleteMany/updateMany + a count check,
  instead of trusting a bare id — closes an IDOR class of bug that a
  single-tenant system never had to worry about.
- Realtime SSE topics ("kitchen"/"pdv") are now per-restaurant
  (`kitchen:${restaurantId}`) so one restaurant's live board never
  sees another's events.
- /totem and /pedir move to /totem/[slug] and /pedir/[slug] — the only
  public screens with no QR Code to resolve a restaurant from. New
  /signup does self-service onboarding (Restaurant + Settings + first
  ADMIN user, auto-login), also used as the isolation test's own
  second-tenant fixture.
- Data migration backfills all pre-existing rows onto one
  'rst_default' restaurant (slug "principal") — the real restaurant
  already in production, preserved verbatim.

Found and fixed during isolation testing: the order-number Counter
row wasn't migrated to its new per-restaurant key, so the first order
placed after the migration collided with an existing order number
(unique constraint violation). Added a small follow-up migration that
renames the counter key, preserving the existing sequence.

Verified: full TypeScript + lint clean, production build clean. A
12-point isolation test (via /signup, creating a real second
restaurant on an isolated DB copy) confirms: empty dashboards for a
new tenant, 404 on cross-tenant IDOR attempts by id, independent
per-restaurant numbering/coupons/audit log, SSE events never leaking
across restaurants, and /totem/[slug] serving only its own menu.
Separately reran the full real-restaurant regression (QR order → PDV
payment → totem → painel → reports) after the fix.

fix(reprice): P1 — split !userId (401) from ownership check (403) on POST /:requestId/reprice (#1913)

## Broken leg
The reprice IDOR fix folded !userId into the ownership 403 branch:

    if (!userId || (br.ownerId !== userId && !isSuperAdminVerified(...))) {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Not authorized to reprice this booking' });
    }

Unauth callers ate a wasted bookingRequests SELECT before hitting a
MISLEADING 403 that suggested a permissions problem, not a
credentials problem. The audit agent classified this as "risky-cosmetic"
because it's a 403→401 client-behavior change; on inspection the reprice
client is always an authenticated logged-in customer, so a 401 only fires
for callers that shouldn't be reaching the endpoint at all.

## Fix (server-only, split into two clean checks)
1. Explicit 401 at the door — before the DB fetch — with an honest
   'Authentication required' message.
2. Ownership check no longer needs the !userId branch — reads cleanly
   as "owner OR verified admin".

Both branches unchanged behaviorally for legitimate callers.

## Test
server/tests/reprice-401-hygiene.regression.test.ts — 3 pins:
  ✓ returns 401 explicitly when there is no userId
  ✓ 401 guard sits BEFORE the first db.select() (no wasted round-trip)
  ✓ ownership check no longer folds !userId into the 403 branch

    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  3 passed (3)

## Dependency
None. Completes the auth-slippage sweep on booking-requests.ts —
prior sweep PRs #1904 (confirm), #1911 (7 POSTs), #1912 (GET). This
covers the last remaining router-mounted handler with the same shape.

## Risk
Very low. 401 replaces 403 for anon callers only (a case that already
denied). Legitimate customer + admin repricing unchanged.

## Do not merge
Per standing CEO directive.

Promotes the consolidated V2 codebase to the production branch:
- Full V1->V2 consolidation (cron POST/QStash support, IDOR fixes,
  MediaAsset atomic claim, TikTok webhook signature verification,
  AI entitlement bypass fix, comment-webhook dedup constraint)
- OAuth state-signature CSRF bypass fix

  httpOnly session cookie replacing localStorage JWT storage, upload
  content magic-byte sniffing, OAuth error-message sanitization
- Landing page / billing / admin dashboard / business-brain / brands work

main's three unique commits (QStash POST support, a cache-bust comment,
and a stacked-decorator fix) are already fully incorporated into
amai-v2-development's own cron.controller.ts, confirmed by diff before
merging.

Security audit hardening: CORS, rate limiting, DTO validation, httpOnly session cookie, upload content-sniffing

Implements the fixes from this session's full security audit (Sections
5-8 plus remaining Section 3/4 items) that weren't already applied live:

- CORS: replace origin:'*' with an explicit allowlist (APP_URL/
  FRONTEND_URL/localhost) in the production Nest bootstrap
  (apps/web/src/lib/backendPort.ts). The previous config also paired
  wildcard origin with credentials:true, an invalid combination per the
  Fetch spec.

- Rate limiting: add @Throttle overrides on auth endpoints (login/
  register/verify/resend/forgot-password/reset-password) and on the two
  AI-generation endpoints, tighter than the app-wide default limiter.

- Server-side validation: convert ~13 inline @Body() object-literal types
  across auth/engine/media/oauth/posts controllers into real
  class-validator DTO classes, closing a gap where NestJS's global
  ValidationPipe silently validated nothing for non-class body types.

- Session storage: move the auth JWT from localStorage (readable by any
  XSS for up to 30 days) to an httpOnly cookie. AuthController.login sets
  it; a new AuthController.logout clears it. JwtStrategy reads it via a
  hand-rolled cookie parser (no new dependency). The frontend now caches
  only a non-sensitive user snapshot (id/email/name/brandId/expiry) for
  synchronous UI checks; apiFetch, the upload flow, the SSE stream, and
  the three OAuth connect links all rely on the cookie traveling
  automatically instead of a client-readable token.

- File upload content-sniffing: verify uploaded bytes actually match
  their claimed MIME type (magic-byte checks for JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP/
  ISOBMFF/EBML) on both the multer path and the direct-to-Blob register
  path, on top of the existing allowlist checks.

- OAuth error handling: stop reflecting err.message into redirect query
  params (info-disclosure risk); log full errors server-side, show
  generic messages to the user. Remove partial-secret and raw-code
  logging in the Instagram token exchange.

Also includes earlier uncommitted work from this session: the OAuth
state-signature CSRF bypass fix, IDOR fixes (createPost media ownership,
media folder parentId), MediaAsset atomic processing claim, TikTok
webhook signature verification, AI entitlement bypass fix, comment-
webhook dedup constraint, and unrelated UI/landing/billing changes.

Verified via full `tsc --noEmit` on apps/api (clean) and TypeScript
syntax-parsing across every edited frontend file; full-project `tsc` on
apps/web does not complete in this sandbox within a reasonable time, so
frontend changes are verified by syntax-parse + manual review rather than
a complete type-check. The JWT/httpOnly-cookie migration specifically has
not been exercised in a live browser this session -- recommend a manual
smoke test (login, logout, file upload, Instagram/TikTok/Drive connect)
before treating it as fully verified.

role guard.

fix(security): IDOR sur les routes environnements — envId jamais vérifié contre le projet de l'URL

Audit de sécurité (Phase 28), suite du fix Platform Requests. Deux routes
récupéraient un environnement par :envId sans jamais vérifier qu'il
appartenait au projet de l'URL (:id) :

- PUT /:id/environments/:envId/link : linkEnvironment() ne vérifie que
  l'EXISTENCE de l'environnement, jamais son project_id — un maintainer du
  projet A pouvait modifier le lien Argo CD d'un environnement du projet B
  en devinant/énumérant son id, malgré loadProjectAccess() qui n'autorise
  que le rôle sur A. Vrai IDOR cross-projet, pré-existant (pas introduit
  cette session).
- POST /:id/environments/:envId/provision-argocd-app (ajoutée cette
  session) : la vérification project_id existait mais pas
  guardProductionEnvironment — un maintainer (pas seulement owner) pouvait
  reconfigurer l'app Argo CD d'un environnement de PRODUCTION, alors que
  sync/rollback/promote l'exigent déjà tous.

Corrigé : les deux routes vérifient désormais explicitement
environment.project_id === req.pgProject.id (404 sinon, jamais confirmer
l'existence d'une ressource hors périmètre) et appellent
guardProductionEnvironment.

l'attaque réelle (projet B créé, maintainer du projet A tente de lier/
provisionner son environnement via l'URL du projet A) — VÉRIFIÉ comme
détectant réellement la régression : `git stash` du correctif fait échouer
ce test précis (1 failed), le correctif restauré le fait passer avec les 9
autres (10/10). Suite complète (123 SQLite + 34 Postgres, 30 e2e), build
frontend.

Security:
- S1 admin dashboard now FAILS CLOSED when no admin allowlist is configured.
  Previously requireAdmin returned the caller as admin when both MCP_ADMIN_EMAILS
  and MCP_ADMIN_MICROSOFT_IDS were unset (with mcpAdminTenantId defaulting to
  'common'), so any Microsoft account in any tenant could read every user's
  meeting content via /admin. (dashboard.ts)
